extracted.intended_audience: students, scholars, and practitioners of journalism and media studies; journalists interested in news selection and newsroom routines
extracted.subtask_description: Analysis of how journalists and news organizations decide which national stories to cover, focusing on values, routines, organizational structures, and external pressures that shape news judgment and story selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Values, professional standards, and external pressures
rubrics_metrics.description: The values, professional standards, and the external pressures that shaped journalists' judgments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gans studies how enduring journalistic values and external factors combine to influence which stories reporters and editors consider newsworthy; applies across multiple headline events (e.g., Vietnam, Watergate).

rubrics_metrics.name: News judgment
rubrics_metrics.description: The basics of news judgment that determine what is selected as national news.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Core principles of news judgment (what counts as important or relevant) are treated as relatively stable determinants of story selection despite later media changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Story selection and story lists
rubrics_metrics.description: How editors, producers, and story selectors compile story lists and choose which items to run.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes routines and personnel (beat reporters, producers and editors, top editors/top producers) involved in generating and trimming story lists and determining placement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Newsworthiness — importance and relevance
rubrics_metrics.description: Criteria of newsworthiness such as whether a story is important, relevant, dramatic, or constitutes disorder.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples in the book include coverage priorities during major events (war, protests, assassinations, scandals) and the prevalence of 'disorder stories' and dramatic narrative forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enduring journalistic values
rubrics_metrics.description: Enduring values that guide coverage decisions (referred to as 'enduring values').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These values are used to explain continuity in news judgment and include implicit norms about what makes a good or legitimate story.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audience considerations (viewers and readers)
rubrics_metrics.description: The role of viewers and readers in shaping what news organizations choose to cover.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Audience tastes, perceived interests, and market considerations influence selection and presentation; tied to concerns about ratings/readership and relevance to national audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sources and reliance on officials
rubrics_metrics.description: The influence of sources — especially public officials, politicians, and institutional sources — on news content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coverage often depends on accessible official sources; source availability and relations with journalists affect which perspectives appear and which stories get prominence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Format and medium constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: How the format (television vs. magazine) and production constraints shape what and how stories are presented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Television journalists face visual/time limits and program formats that privilege certain kinds of stories; magazines have different rhythms and space for analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organizational and corporate pressures
rubrics_metrics.description: Corporate, advertiser, and organizational influences on newsroom decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ownership, advertiser relationships, and corporate structure can exert pressure on editorial priorities and story selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiperspectival and analytical coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: The extent to which coverage incorporates multiple perspectives and analysis ('multiperspectival').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gans examines whether news organizations provide plural viewpoints and analytical depth versus narrow or official-dominated accounts.

rubrics_metrics.name: News as a symbolic arena
rubrics_metrics.description: The role of national news media as a symbolic arena reflecting nation and society.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stories are not only informational but symbolic — media participation helps shape national discourse, identity, and what is considered politically or socially salient.
